# ruststream-rumqttc

> `ruststream-rumqttc` is the MQTT 5 broker crate for RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them. Over the `rumqttc` client it subscribes a service to topics and topic filters, publishes with a declared quality of service and retain flag, and carries headers as MQTT 5 user properties, so non-Rust peers see plain MQTT messages.

A subscription is a descriptor: `MqttTopic` for one topic, `MqttFilter` for a topic filter with wildcards, each with its own quality of service and share group; a bare string in `#[subscriber("..")]` is a topic. A routes file imports `ruststream_rumqttc::prelude::*`, which offers `MqttPublish` as `Publish`; a body that changes the quality of service or the retain flag of one message takes a step from `MqttPublishSteps`. An MQTT broker keeps one retained message per topic and the unacknowledged messages of a persistent session, and the framework's runtime supplies the rest, such as delayed retries.

This site holds the guides, one page per component and the architecture of the crate; the API reference is on docs.rs, and the framework itself is documented on the RustStream site.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/): building an MQTT 5 service with the crate, from a first subscriber to a production server
- [Getting started](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/getting-started/): installation, a local Mosquitto, a first subscriber against it and its test without a server
- [Topics, wildcards and shared subscriptions](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/topics/): topic design, many topics through `+` and `#`, work shared between replicas in a share group, and overlapping filters
- [Delivery guarantees](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/delivery/): the quality of service, what each handler outcome sends, a persistent session across restarts and the deliveries in flight
- [Device state: retained messages and the last will](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/device-state/): each device's current state kept on the server, clearing it, and the service's online status through a last will
- [Publishing commands](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/publishing/): a command to one device out of many, the quality of service per message, and headers as MQTT 5 properties
- [Retries and dead letters](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/retries/): a retry now or later, the attempt cap, the dead-letter topic, and the copies of a filter sent back to their own topics
- [Request and response](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/request-response/): answers on the response topic each request names, with its correlation data, and a fixed topic as the fallback
- [Testing an MQTT service](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/testing/): `TestApp` on the production app with wildcard topics, published alerts and delays, and the same test on Mosquitto
- [Connecting to production](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/guides/production/): credentials, TLS with a client certificate, one client id per process, limits, reconnects and a configuration test

## Components

- [Components](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/): the parts of the crate an MQTT service uses, one page each
- [MqttBroker](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/): the broker type, its URL and client id, and its lazy connection
- [Security](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/security/): the login in the URL or `credentials`, `tls_ca` and `tls_client_auth`
- [Session](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/session/): `clean_start(false)` and `session_expiry`, a session the server keeps between connections
- [last_will](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/last-will/): the message the server publishes when the connection ends without a clean disconnect
- [Limits](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/limits/): `max_packet_size` and `receive_maximum`, the packet size cap and the flow-control window
- [Reconnect](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/reconnect/): `reconnect` and its modes (the client's own from 100 ms to 5 s by default, never, a custom `Reconnector`), the resubscribe, and `keep_alive`
- [Startup](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/startup/): the wait for the server's `CONNACK`, and the refusals that fail it at once
- [Shutdown](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/shutdown/): the clean `DISCONNECT`, and `MqttError::NotConnected` for a publisher used afterwards
- [Prelude](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/prelude/): `ruststream_rumqttc::prelude`, the one glob an MQTT service imports
- [Errors](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/broker/errors/): `MqttError`, the one error type of the crate
- [Subscriptions](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/): a topic in `#[subscriber]` and the descriptors that carry every other setting
- [MqttTopic](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/mqtt-topic/): one topic with no wildcard, which answers for its own retry copies
- [MqttFilter](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/mqtt-filter/): a topic filter with the `+` and `#` wildcards
- [Qos](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/qos/): at most once, at least once or exactly once, and the level a delivery arrives at
- [shared](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/shared/): a share group, where the server hands each message to one member
- [Overlaps](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/overlaps/): overlapping filters on one connection, told apart by subscription identifiers
- [Batches](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/batches/): slice handlers over batches the crate assembles on the client
- [Lanes](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/subscriptions/lanes/): `workers(n, by_key)`, keyed by the `partition-key` header the publisher sets, in order per key
- [Acknowledgement](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/): what an `ack` and a `drop` send at each quality of service
- [retry](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/retry/): a delivery left unacknowledged until a persistent session resumes
- [retry_after](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/retry-after/): a copy the runtime publishes after a delay, within the session
- [Retries](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/retries/): `max_attempts`, counted on the framework's retry-count header
- [Dead letters](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/dead-letters/): `dead_letter`, the topic a delivery that reached its cap goes to
- [out_retry](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/settlement/out-retry/): where the retry copies of a filter subscription go, once or per delivery
- [MqttContext](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/context/): the topic a delivery was published to, read through `Ctx<DeliveryTopic>`
- [MqttPublish](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/publishing/): the publish policy, `Publish` in the prelude, with its QoS and retain flag
- [MqttPublishSteps](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/publishing/mqtt-publish-steps/): the `qos` and `retain` steps of one message
- [Retained](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/publishing/retained/): a message the server keeps on its topic for later subscribers
- [Headers](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/publishing/headers/): headers as MQTT 5 user properties, and the three that take the protocol's own properties
- [Responders](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/publishing/responders/): a handler that answers on the response topic of each request
- [MQTT bindings](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/asyncapi/): the `mqtt` bindings of the AsyncAPI document behind the `asyncapi` feature
- [Server](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/asyncapi/server/): the server's host and port and the session the client opens, never credentials
- [Operations](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/asyncapi/operations/): the QoS of a receive operation, and the QoS and retain flag of a send operation
- [Messages](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/asyncapi/messages/): the MQTT 5 properties each message rides
- [Replies](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/asyncapi/replies/): a reply address read from the `reply-to` header of the request
- [Testing](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/testing/): `TestApp::start` with `MqttBroker` on an in-process MQTT server behind the `testing` feature
- [Live](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/components/testing/live/): `TestApp::start_live`, the same test body against a running MQTT server

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/): how MQTT 5 works, where the crate sits between the server and the RustStream runtime, and what that costs
- [Topics](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/mqtt/): topics, filters, share groups and retained messages on an MQTT server
- [Quality of service](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/mqtt/qos/): the QoS 1 and QoS 2 flows, the receive window, and what a publish keeps across a reconnect
- [Sessions](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/mqtt/sessions/): a session's subscriptions and unacknowledged messages, keep-alive and the last will
- [Design](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/design/): one connection and one task between the runtime and the `rumqttc` client
- [Lifecycle](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/lifecycle/): `new`, `connect`, the subscriptions at startup, the reconnect and the `DISCONNECT` at shutdown
- [Path](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/path/): one message from the event loop through the handler and the reply to its acknowledgement
- [Demultiplexing](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/demultiplexing/): subscription identifiers for overlapping filters, and subscriptions taking turns on one filter
- [Settlement](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/settlement/): what `ack`, drop, retry and `retry_after` become on MQTT
- [Benchmarks](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/benchmarks/): what the crate and the framework's runtime cost over the raw `rumqttc` client, and the cost of the crate's own code
- [Benchmarks: Numbers](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/benchmarks/numbers/): what each published number measures, and what it does not allow you to conclude
- [Benchmarks: Methodology](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-rumqttc/latest/architecture/benchmarks/methodology/): the three loops, the run on a real MQTT server and the code count with `just bench`
